mainClaim: Removing standardized tests reduces equity and makes admissions more subjective and biased
evidence: No verified source is cited for this argument. The argument rests on reasoning: a common test gives admissions staff one measure that is comparable across schools, while recommendation letters, extracurriculars and grades vary with school resources.
supportingPoints: Tests provide standardized measure across vastly different school districts
Free test prep resources have improved dramatically (Khan Academy SAT prep)
High-achieving low-income students benefit most from test score visibility
Holistic review without tests amplifies implicit bias in admissions
limitations: The earlier University of California study and its figures could not be traced to a published source and were removed. Other figures in the supporting points have not been checked. Doesn't address fundamental issues with test design and access to prep. Cultural bias in tests remains a concern. Suggests reform rather than elimination.
